newsitem.title: GERMANY: Prodi says Kohl has no problems with Italy in EMU.
newsitem.headline: Prodi says Kohl has no problems with Italy in EMU.

text.p: Italian Prime Minister Romano Prodi said on Thursday after a meeting with Chancellor Helmut Kohl that the German leader had no objections to Italy joining the exchange rate mechanism and then the single European currency.
Prodi said Kohl told him, "From the government side and from him, there would be no obstacles to the re-entry of the lira into the exchange rate mechanism and then into the single European currency."
Prodi was speaking to journalists after dining with Kohl in Bonn during an evening visit to the German seat of government before returning to Rome.

Prodi said the Maastricht Treaty, which outlines the ground rules for currency union set to start in January 1999, made clear that Italy would have to join the exchange rate mechanism (ERM) by the end of the year to qualify for monetary union.
He said the treaty made clear "that any currency had to join the ERM two years before the start of monetary union".

Bundesbank President Hans Tietmeyer also said earlier on Thursday in a briefing to Swedish reporters in Frankfurt that the treaty was "very clear" that membership in the exchange rate mechanism was a condition for entry into currency union.
In addition, Prodi said Kohl was supportive of Rome's efforts to play a central role in European affairs.
"Germany views very positively a strong Italian presence in European institutions," Prodi said.
